title: Diagnose Mixologist reaction marker placement and clearing failures
description: Graphical storybook_mixologist_reaction_scene_test.gd fails the recipient-only, automatic-clear and next-battle cleanup assertions on both pristine 61de0d3 and the olr-05o branch. Reproduced using isolated user data and Godot 4.7.2. Root cause is not established.
acceptance_criteria: Establish the cause and verify correct marker placement and lifetime across battle transitions without weakening the intended behavior.
close_reason: Whole-tile graphical comparisons counted unrelated cast animation. Isolated the real reaction ink without changing runtime behavior. Verified recipient placement, expiry, and battle transition; wrong-target and stuck-marker mutations fail, and three independent graphical runs plus Alchemist and rules suites pass.

title: Diagnose Ferryman terminal replay safe-bank timing failure
description: The graphical ferryman_adventure_scene_test.gd reaches the rescue replay but never observes safe_bank before its seven-second watch expires on this environment, including an idle display. Reproduced independently on pristine 61de0d3 and the commission fixture for olr-05o. Distinguish runtime playback from test harness or renderer timing; do not weaken the assertion without establishing the actual behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Explain the cause and verify that the full safe-bank clip is observable in a real commission rescue replay.

title: Order of Last Resort: add a persistent combat grid visibility toggle
description: Let the player hide or show the visible battlefield grid during combat, independently of nameplate visibility. This changes only the grid overlay, not movement, targeting, or tile selection.
acceptance_criteria: Switch the grid off and back on without leaving combat; the overlay updates immediately. The choice persists across fights and game restarts. Changing it leaves the nameplate setting and tile interactions unchanged.

title: Order of Last Resort: adjust combat nameplates and add a persistent visibility toggle
description: Ronald finds the nameplates clash visually with the character models. Compare possible adjustments in the same combat scene so he can choose a direction; no specific visual fix has been selected. Separately, let him hide or show nameplates without leaving combat.
acceptance_criteria: Review the current and proposed nameplates alongside the models at gameplay scale, then apply the chosen adjustment. During combat, toggling nameplates off or on immediately updates their visibility. The chosen setting carries into subsequent fights and survives quitting and relaunching the game.

title: Add in-game help and tutorials to Barnaby's Order of Last Resort
description: Help new players learn the game formerly called Company of Unlikely Heroes without consulting the README. Guide them through founding a guild, choosing a commission, and playing their first battle. Provide on-demand help for returning players.
acceptance_criteria: Players can skip or replay the tutorials, look up controls and objectives during play, and close help without losing their place. From Help, players can open a dedicated Godot Engine credits page that says “Made with Godot Engine,” thanks the Godot contributors, and links to the official MIT license page at https://godotengine.org/license/.

title: Choose an audio approach: scripted, AI-generated, or hybrid
description: Start with one frequent gameplay sound. Compare synthesizing it from code, generating an editable audio clip, and using a clip with scripted playback variation. Consider timing, creative control, repeat fatigue, cost, and rights to ship. Treat music as a separate decision. This bead scopes a listening test; it does not authorize paid generation or game integration.
acceptance_criteria: Agree with Ronald on a representative cue and a low-cost listening test. Judge candidates at matched loudness, both once and in a repeated gameplay rhythm. Record which approach to try first and why, or what evidence is missing.

title: Company: Retire the seven legacy fixed adventures
description: Remove the original fixed route definitions, --fixed-outings launcher and outing-only runtime paths. Retire the adventures as sequences, not the individual missions or shared commission mechanics. Migrate useful playable regression recipes to standalone mission launches before dropping outing-only tests.
acceptance_criteria: No shipped fixed-outing route or picker remains. Active commissions and retained standalone missions still launch; current docs and tests no longer require the old adventures. Preserve historical experiment records.
notes:
em7 handoff: Mixologist and stock cast regression entrypoints now use public standalone --mission [--party] [--loadout]; retain those checks. Before removing first_outing, replace commission_settings.roster_adventure as the live source of the commission recruitment roster and verify normal recruitment/guild loadouts. The new standalone launcher itself does not need a fixed adventure.
ojr handoff: commission_scene_test.gd and tools/capture_guild_book.gd inherit village_outing_scene_test.gd for shared battle/UI helpers. Preserve or extract that support before deleting fixed-outing tests; rerun the commission tests and documented seed-6 guild-book capture.
close_reason: Removed all seven fixed sequences, picker and outing-only runtime. Preserved all 20 missions, commission roster/loadouts and playable victory recipes. Verified 42 headless suites, graphical inventory for all 20 missions, and complete seed-6 commission capture; affected checks rerun after test refinements. Two separately reproduced baseline graphical failures tracked as olr-r0z and olr-gpv.

title: Company: Launch a mission with chosen heroes and loadouts from the CLI
description: Extend the existing --mission=<id> isolated battle launch for interactive playtesting. Accept an ordered party and optional per-hero loadouts using existing game identifiers and legal build rules. Support missions that normally obtain their party from recruitment; do not require a fixed outing or a guild save.
acceptance_criteria: Document runnable examples for a custom party with default and explicit loadouts. Tests verify the requested party, order and builds at battle start and restart, helpful errors for invalid selections, existing authored defaults where available, and no guild progression or save changes.
close_reason: Standalone CLI launches ordered parties and legal partial per-hero builds without guild saves or outings. Migrated Mixologist and stock cast regression entrypoints. 27 launcher cases plus graphical and compatibility checks passed.

title: Company: Remove Practice outings from normal play
description: Remove practice navigation from guild creation, commission board, profile recovery and any return paths. Keep commission play intact. Reconcile practice-specific criteria in open polish beads ddd.14, .15, .16, .20 and .22 so they do not reintroduce practice.
acceptance_criteria: Normal launch, recovery and return flows never expose practice. Scene tests and capture scripts exercise the remaining real-game routes.
close_reason: Removed Practice navigation from normal guild creation, commission board, recovery and return paths. Migrated scene regressions and screenshot capture to playable commissions and reconciled five polish beads. Verified five scene suites and the complete 17-image graphical capture.

title: Explore how to share Barnaby's Order of Last Resort as a playable web link
description: Investigate the path from Barnaby's Order of Last Resort (formerly Company of Unlikely Heroes) to a browser playtest. Explain what WebAssembly runs, what other files Godot exports, and what the host must serve. Check this game's Godot version, renderer, and dependencies for web compatibility. Research only; do not publish the game or provision hosting.
acceptance_criteria: Document a recommended hosting option and its requirements, project-specific blockers or unknowns, and the smallest local browser test that would verify the recommendation.

title: Company: Design the Blacksmith
description: Pursue closest opponent. Back Off deals 1 damage and pushes. Try This reverses abilities, e.g. Knight push becomes pull, guard becomes area push, Wizard blast becomes healing. Lower priority because each interaction needs design and validation. Source: .lore/work/games/company-of-unlikely-heroes/notes/hero-class-pitches.md. Design only.
acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate the Knight pairing, define recipients and duration, and assess reversal coverage before committing to roster-wide support.

title: Company: Investigate a new art direction
description: Compare alternatives with the existing art notes and boards in .lore/work/games/company-of-unlikely-heroes/notes/. Consider how heroes, obstacles and threatened tiles read at actual play size.
acceptance_criteria: Record the visual trade-offs and Ronald’s preferred direction or reason to keep exploring. No asset production or integration.

title: Company: Design mechanically distinct hero classes
description: Treat Blast Knight and Alchemist as mix-ins, not the bar for a new class. Explore heroes whose offense, utility and personal habit create a new decision under hybrid orders.
acceptance_criteria: For each shortlisted class, describe a turn where bringing it changes the plan, and why reassigning existing abilities would not achieve the same thing.
notes: Ronald's five pitches and design audit: .lore/work/games/company-of-unlikely-heroes/notes/hero-class-pitches.md. Includes the proposed Alchemist replacement, Bard song-weaving progression, and both Necromancer minion kits. Suggested first paper check: Rogue swap and blame in the rescue. No class selected or authorized for implementation.
